You pay good hard cash to buy your letters, then form a word to sell at a profit, if you can. Your payoff depends on the quantity and the quality of the letters in your word. BuyWord mixes basic mathematics, money management, and good old-fashioned word-building in a simple, yet elegant blend that keeps every player involved in every turn until the very end. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Setup Each player starts with 200 dollars. Each players gets 8 wild tiles for 1 player, 4 for 2 players, 3 for 3 players and 2 for 4 players. Gameplay At the start of each round, a die is thrown. The number on it is the number of tiles drawn by each player this round. If it is “choice”, the first player chooses a number from 2 to 5. Starting from the first player, each player may buy all or none of their drawn tiles. If you choose to buy all, pay an amount of money equal to the square of the total number of pips on them. Otherwise, discard them. Starting from the first player, each player may sell any number of words. If you want to play a word, discard the tiles needed and get an amount of money equal to the square of the total number of pips on them. A wild tile counts as any letter, but each word may only have one wild. At the end of the round, each player must discard down to 8 letters, excluding wilds. Afterwards, the last player becomes the first player and a new round is started. End of the Game The last round starts when the last letter is drawn. If the tiles drawn cannot satisfy the requirements, they are all discarded. After all players sell their last words, the player with the most money wins. [Rating: 2/10] I'm not much for word games, but this was a little bit interesting inside of its genre. I just don't care for its genre.

[Rating: 2/10] Sell Word, if I can manage it.  Did I mention I'm not a fan of word games?  Gameplay encourages long words instead of gaming small words for word/letter bonuses in Scrabble.  Shorter than Scrabble. It doesn't leave me feeling like killing myself halfway through.

[Rating: 2/10] As word games go, this is pretty interesting and unusual! But it's also pretty bland and there is no point to the other players being there whatsoever.

[Rating: 2/10] This game feels like a waste of energy. We've played this a handful of times (all 2-player), and the scores have been so close each time that they feel inevitable. I can't tell what constitutes a mistake, or a clever play. Without feedback there's nothing but the satisfaction of making words, and the hand limit of ten tiles sorely restricts the possibilities. There are better word games.

[Rating: 3/10] I got this game because buying and selling letters to make words sounded cool (I like Scrabble; I like economic games). The problem is, someone forgot to mention that this isn't a game - there is zero player interaction, the only real skill is making words, there is no money management involved. Any of the variants might make this a real game, but they seem like obvious off-the-cuff suggestions rather than playtested variants (the "auction" variant, the most promising avenue to turn this into a real game, is the one that is obviously the most non-functional). [Rating: 3/10] The game is so short that luck of the draw can ruin it.  This really wasn't thought through properly

[Rating: 3/10] (2-4 players) I haven't quite figured this game out yet but want to play it more to get good at it. Unfortunately, you can't squeak by with short words like you can in Scrabble. Here it's all about the big words.

[Rating: 3/10] An economic word game. First play I thought this was clever. On follow-up plays less so. There may be a good variant here somewhere if you give the game enough time

[Rating: 3/10] I don't know, wasn't a fan of this game and I love word games. I'd rather play stuff like So Clover or Cross Clues than that. I think it is an interesting concept however but it is more about making long words and being good at maths than anything else. I can't be bothered counting if I made a profit with that word or not so definitely not a game for me.

[Rating: 3.6/10] interresting wordgame. where you buy smaller amount of letters to make a bigger word later...

[Rating: 4/10] I hate to demean the memory of one of the hobbies founders.  But truly, what is the hubbub about here.  A rather lifeless Scrabble variant.

[Rating: 4/10] I suppose Scrabble nuts would enjoy it more, but there's really nothing there other than making words. And it literally is multiplayer solitare.

[Rating: 4/10] Not sure exactly why, but this game completely bombed with my Scrabble-loving friends. Most of them seemed to not "get it" and ended up becoming frustrated. I may experiment with starting off with more cash if I'm allowed to play again...!
